avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, and the fight against emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and it pays an organization to green private and institutional land. Boroughs are adding their own resources: money from the parks fund, equipment rental, and blue-collar worker crews. Exemptions also apply to tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for parks purposes to buy trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont awards URBEX Construction inc. the contract to renovate the parc Pratt chalet and redevelop its surroundings, including planting vegetation, funded in part by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain, for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees there for planting.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives and clean streets, sidewalks and bike paths. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, the sidewalk cleaning contract for four private snow removal sectors is awarded to Les Équipements Benco Canada ltée for $271,979.11, taxes included [CA26 27 0034].

etapes.titre: Maintenance and snow removal of public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is hiring companies to remove snow, spread abrasives and maintain downtown public squares, including Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord pays $106,150.97 more for renting an additional grader [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard draws $200,000 from its surpluses to pay staff and buy salt and sand [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offers city council to provide its own staff for its snow disposal site.

The City is extending turnkey snow removal contracts for twelve months in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, towing contracts in four boroughs, and equipment rentals with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Boroughs are doing the same for their own machine rentals.

aSurveiller.texte: The extended towing contracts for Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension start on November 15, 2026.
The eight turnkey snow removal contracts awarded in August cover four winter seasons and end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: The City is financing and building the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, and is awarding several contracts for maintenance and upgrades to this plant. It is also having water and sewer pipes rehabilitated or rebuilt in many boroughs, with replacement of lead service connections, on both the public side and the private side. Loan by-laws govern the financing of this work.

etapes.titre: Lead water service connections taken over by boroughs
etapes.texte: Lachine, Le Sud-Ouest and Ahuntsic-Cartierville are offering city council to carry out, themselves, the replacement of lead service connections located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the owners.

etapes.titre: New loans and addition to an ongoing contract
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council is adopting a loan of $12,000,000 for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector. It is adding $12,144,522.14 in contingencies to Pomerleau's contract for the pipe on rue de la Cathédrale, toward the McTavish reservoir, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019.

aSurveiller.texte: Adoption planned for October 19, 2026 of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
Commissioning of the ozone plant planned for 2029; the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 must end in the last quarter of 2028.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 starting the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, about six weeks each.
Rehabilitation of the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord and the Atwater ramp to be completed no later than December 18, 2026.
End of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe postponed from December 2026 to March 2027.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned landfill, transformed into a park by phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrade.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back: a greenhouse complex in the park's southwest sector, the upgrade of the electrical facilities at the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel, and the park's routine maintenance. It also requested funding from Québec for a trail crossing the park from east to west, and launched the redevelopment of rue De Louvain along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for an east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use trail crossing the park from east to west, with a footbridge about 150 metres long. The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow [CG26 0121].

etapes.titre: Green light for the greenhouse project
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration approves the construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform: 1,500 m² for research and training, 1,000 m² for the Saint-Michel neighbourhood's community greenhouse, with a construction budget estimated at $2,185,000 [CG26 0124]. The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry out the project, and city council agrees.

etapes.titre: Site electrical system and park maintenance
etapes.texte: The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. the second phase of electrical works at the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel, for $1,091,693.37 taxes included: a new 25 kV supply, transformer, backup generator and a controller to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223]. It also awards Groupe Nicky and Entreprises Roseneige the general upkeep and ecological and horticultural management of the park, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028 [CG26 0224].

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 taxes included. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings, in three phases from 2026 to 2028.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator, from June 20 to October 15, 2026, for an additional expense of $296,349.21 taxes included. The compost is used as soil amendment, in particular for the development of parc Frédéric-Back [CG26 0320].

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the ministère des Transports funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, closes on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouse installation work is to be completed by December 2026, with commissioning announced for winter 2027.
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, curb extensions), then from May to August 2028 (final pavement, bike path, plantings).
The park maintenance contracts run until October 31, 2028, with two possible 12-month extensions.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, in the making: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.texte: The City added $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones needing hand cleaning, a larger quantity of mortar and a deteriorated culvert account for the increase.

The City authorized the submission of the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for DarkSky International's Urban Night Sky Place international designation. The application requires no financial commitment; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan and bringing its light fixtures up to standard.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as protected natural areas
etapes.texte: The City listed the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, with conservation plans providing for ecological management. It also took note of the 2025 report on the areas.

The City awarded Gendron Gestion Civil inc. a contract to reconstruct the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45, taxes included. The culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

aSurveiller.texte: The Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan must be submitted in February 2027, DarkSky International's response is expected in April 2027, and full site compliance is set for April 2032.
The snow removal contract covers two winters, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
The janitorial services contract for the nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with an option to extend until October 31, 2031.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City is lending municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres during the 2025-2026 winter. It is also funding community organizations working on homelessness, extending to other boroughs a public works team managed by Ville-Marie, and setting up a framework to receive private donations. Near the end of the period, it purchases services to help people from the campements on rue Notre-Dame transition toward housing.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations that will host people experiencing homelessness there: the former church at 5600, 12e Avenue in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, the former Recluses Missionaries monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est and the former Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert. The loans run until April 30, 2026, and the City covers energy costs and technical maintenance of the sites.

etapes.titre: Borough funding for warming centres and outreach
etapes.texte: Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is confirming a contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre, and Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is transferring $250,000 for the setup of the Bain Saint-Denis warming centre.

Council adopts a mechanism governing private cash donations for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects: donors do not choose which project is funded, and the City can refuse a donation. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on rent support.

The City grants $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to help people from the campements on rue Notre-Dame transition toward shelter and housing, from July 13 to October 18, 2026. It pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the Nuit des sans-abri, and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling on the campements under the viaduc Van Horne.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate near the campements on rue Notre-Dame ends on October 18, 2026.
The public works team agreement with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.
Support for the Nuit des sans-abri covers the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the lease of a piece of land to the Société de transport de Montréal for the parking of its officers' vehicles, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. It is also extending the lease of a neighbouring piece of land to a company for paid parking reserved for members of an app.

The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is awarding a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The main street becomes avenue des Solidarités
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the écoquartier "avenue des Solidarités". The name comes from a public call for suggestions held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding a contract to build a road with sewer, water main, roadway, electrical network and lighting in the écoquartier, as well as for the environmental management of the soils. It is adding $2,007,312.15 net, from the environmental liability reserve, to rehabilitate the soils of the former gas station area on the Louvain Est site.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, then the construction of a group of buildings with a minimum density of 200 dwelling units per hectare. It is also launching a draft by-law to increase the height and density allowed on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the land rented to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The free loan of the land for growing sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The free loan of the community garden land continues until December 31, 2027.
The land at the corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade would be loaned for programming activities from April 1 to October 31, 2027.

The work on rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The street naming file indicates that site developments are planned for around 2032 and that four other public places still need to be named.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: This year, the City is preparing the ground, both literally and financially, for the future neighbourhood on the site of the former racetrack. It obtained more time from the Québec government to sell a first piece of land, guaranteed a loan for studies, and adopted two loan by-laws for streets, sewers and waterworks in the sector. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, located west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. According to the file, the postponement does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 deed of transfer remain the same.

City council approves a $2,000,000 guarantee from the City in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to the organization GALOPH that will be used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and asset management in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Project for four buildings on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four buildings, in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur, one of which is to house a municipal sports and leisure centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public facilities and equipment in the sector, and a public consultation meeting will be held.

aSurveiller.texte: The sale of a first piece of land must be completed by October 31, 2027 at the latest.
The federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031.
The temporary leases end on April 30, 2027 (MultiCaf), March 31, 2028 (Polliflora) and April 30, 2028 (transition nursery).

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is having parks designed and redone in several boroughs: construction contracts, soil studies, funding for decontamination, and additional funds for projects already underway. It is also active in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, with work on the chemin de Senneville, snow clearing and maintenance contracts, and steps to protect natural environments and the night sky.

etapes.texte: The borough councils are awarding contracts to redo parks: Lucie-Bruneau dog park in Anjou, Mackenzie-King in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Monseigneur-Langlois in Verdun, Percy-Walters in Ville-Marie, Denise-Morelle and Baldwin in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal. The work includes play areas, water play features, trails, furniture and plantings.

The City and the boroughs are adjusting contracts already awarded: supervision of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois, contingencies for parc Villeray, budget transfers for parc des Hirondelles and parc du Sault-au-Récollet, additional fees for parc Denise-Morelle. The City is also paying $168,472.14, net of taxes, to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension for the environmental rehabilitation of parc George-Vernot [CM26 0887].

etapes.titre: Land transferred to parks and school agreement
etapes.texte: A section of the former rue Eadie, measuring 810.2 m², is being transferred from the public street domain to the public park domain to be added to parc Campbell Ouest [CM26 0704]. Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is requesting the same change for a 75.2 m² strip of laneway in parc Le Prévost. Outremont is ratifying an agreement with the Centre de services scolaire Marguerite-Bourgeoys and paying $150,000 for the parc-école Saint-Germain.

aSurveiller.texte: Executive committee on October 7, 2026 and city council on October 19, 2026 on the change of status of the laneway strip at parc Le Prévost.
Work at parc Denise-Morelle is to begin in early August 2026 and end in November 2026.
For the Urban Night Sky Place application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, DarkSky's response expected in April 2027, site compliance by April 2032.
For the public art at parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner selected in October 2026, contract in December 2026, artwork installation in 2028.
Final acceptance of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027; work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc until June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial activity ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares. They are adopting funding rules, paying out money to business development corporations, and then enacting ordinances that close streets to cars and regulate sales, noise and use of the roadway. At the end of the season, reopening schedules are adjusted and two files concern the status and name of public squares.

etapes.titre: Settlement of a dispute over a public square
etapes.texte: The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough settles out of court, for $41,686.46, a lawsuit related to the development work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer. The settlement is concluded without admission of liability.

etapes.titre: Rules and money for the 2026 season
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that sets the conditions for grants to its business development corporations for pedestrianizing streets, with applications due no later than February 16, 2026. The executive committee then authorizes transfers of $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries.

The boroughs pay out amounts to business development corporations and their projects: $102,045 for rue Villeray, $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe. Outremont allocates $105,000, net of taxes, to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awards a contract worth $287,724.94, taxes included, to provide on-demand transportation for people with reduced mobility and seniors on avenue du Mont-Royal, and bans amplified instruments on its pedestrian streets. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve temporarily removes 113 paid parking spaces, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a commercial promotion on a closed street on avenue de Monkland, and the City pays $40,000 to animate the Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street.

etapes.titre: Status, name and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre lot, at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier, from a street (public square) to a local park, and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque « place Chez-Marguerite ». Le Plateau-Mont-Royal divides avenue du Mont-Royal into three sections with separate reopening dates.

aSurveiller.texte: Reopening of avenue du Mont-Royal: between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Full reopening of avenue Bernard to traffic starting September 25, 2026.
The pedestrian streets and public squares of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (avenue Royal, avenue Madison, Placette CDN) remain closed to cars until October 31, 2026.
Boroughs' accountability reporting in November 2026 and return of unspent amounts in December 2026.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period up to December 31, 2027; the contribution for avenue Lacombe runs until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law on the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates lodging establishments and services for people in residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration programs. A public meeting was held on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation took place from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and site coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the heights allowed on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extensions to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, certificates of authorization and cadastral operations. Following the public consultation on March 25, 2026, the City revised the plans for view corridors and heights; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and makes certain work subject to approval in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

etapes.titre: Corrections and next steps on demolitions
etapes.texte: Saint-Léonard acknowledges two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public consultation meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's police department (Service de police de la Ville de Montréal): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The City adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized public safety equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team on enforcing the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys patrol motorcycles, extends the headquarters' housekeeping contract by one year, and awards a contract to replace the oil heating system at the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It authorizes a second loan of a police officer to the RCMP, starting March 30, 2026, with an additional budget of $136,260 for 2026.

etapes.titre: Meals for detainees and call-handling software
etapes.texte: The City awards a company the preparation and delivery of meals for people detained by the SPVM, for three years. It also extends the maintenance of the patrol dispatch and emergency call software by twelve months, and accepts a $8,000 federal grant for a sexual assault awareness campaign.

After the shooting on June 22, 2026 in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, borough councils adopt motions of support for the SPVM. They offer condolences to the families and reaffirm their commitment to the police service.

aSurveiller.texte: Agreement to second police officers to the RCMP's Integrated Synthetic Drug Enforcement Team, starting October 12, 2026, for three years.
"Fèves au lard" (baked beans) day at neighbourhood station 46, on October 23, 2026, for which the Anjou borough is buying tickets.
Start of the lease for the metro unit of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, on February 1, 2027.
Delivery of the port patrol boat and its trailer no later than March 1, 2027.
Completion of the heating replacement work at the cavalry building, expected September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.

etapes.texte: The City sells a 364.3-square-metre plot of land for $495,150 to expand the entrance building of the Place-Saint-Henri station, land in Verdun for $257,425 to rebuild and expand the Rielle ventilation plant, and commits to selling a plot of about 202.8 square metres on rue Jean-Brillant for $115,000 to build a rectifier station there. These amounts are shown before applicable taxes.

Elected officials approve several STM loan by-laws and the corresponding changes to the 2026-2035 capital works program. They cover reserved lanes and priority traffic lights for buses, the rehabilitation of metro and surface infrastructure, cybersecurity, extending the service life of the MR-73 train cars and the analysis of their replacement.

The City purchases advertising space in the STM network and at Astral for Espace pour la vie, for a maximum of $172,462.50, taxes included, and grants $382,000 to the STM to strengthen service during the 2026 UCI Road World Championships. The executive committee accepts the loan of the archaeological collection from the REM excavations; councils adopt motions on preserving the blue line's tunnel boring machine and on a structuring public transit project in the east end.

aSurveiller.texte: The Ahuntsic-Cartierville parking lease starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, for a maximum of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation plant, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; the work is planned to continue until March 2028.
The opening of the five new blue line stations is planned for 2031; the City's work there is integrated in 2028-2029.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the bike-sharing service.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorized a $100,000 expense, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives used notably on bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awarded a $153,395.05 contract, taxes included, for the rental of a mini sweeper with operator that cleans, in spring, paths less than 1.8 metres wide.

etapes.titre: BIXI bikes and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61, taxes included, to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for mechanical bikes, electric-assist bikes, stations and docking points compatible with BIXI. It also added $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for lights, civil and electrical works, and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.

City council approved an agreement for $125,167.62, taxes included, to pay Hydro-Québec the 2014 to 2025 rents for land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approved a 10-year lease, starting January 1, 2026, for a plot of about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, at a total rent of $46,896, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Repairs to the REV Lajeunesse and avenue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offered to take charge of repairs to sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepted this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike lane work. Outremont gave a notice of motion to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: The UCI Road World Championships are being held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; roadway work is planned along the route in Ville-Marie.
Complete financial assistance applications for the rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier projects must be submitted by October 9, 2026, at the latest.
